name: REST: Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding
problem: Draft models are needed just to make speculative decoding work; they require training, storage, and maintenance, and are hard to obtain for arbitrary target models.
mechanism: DRAFT WITH RETRIEVAL instead of with a model. Maintains a datastore of text-to-token-index continuations (Suffix-Array-based self-drafting datastore built from the target model's own training corpus, plus a tree-structured retrieval). At each step the datastore is queried by matching the last few generated tokens against its keys and retrieving the most frequent continuations as draft candidates; the target model verifies them in parallel under the standard modified rejection sampling rule. Plug-and-play, training-free, and adds no draft-model weights.
speedup_reported: 1.62x-2.36x on code or text generation, measured on 7B and 13B models in a SINGLE-BATCH setting, with no draft-model training. Baseline is plain autoregressive decoding of the same model. Both the single-batch caveat and the model size are load-bearing: this is the only record here whose baseline needs no extra model at all, so the speedup is attributable purely to draft quality.
notes: ADOPTION, honestly: NOT in any production engine. It is a neat and much-cited idea (drafting from a retrieval datastore rather than a model) but the datastore must be built per-corpus and the speedup is 1.6-2.4x where EAGLE-3 reports up to 6.5x, so it has been superseded in practice by learned draft models. Included because it is the only clean test of 'how much of speculative decoding's gain is the draft model?' - the answer being about half of EAGLE-3's headline. VENUE: NAACL 2024 per the arXiv comment field ('NAACL 2024, camera ready'); Semantic Scholar could not be reached at verification time due to rate limiting, so venue rests on the arXiv comment alone.
